page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v6 is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at 3.7 GHz. It provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. Memory allocation is 672.0 GB of RAM, equating to 7.0 GB per virtual core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration features like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data reflects strong computing and data handling throughput. In synthetic CPU evaluations, the E96as_v6 achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 147518.16, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-core performance reached 3077.57 in stress-ng, categorizing it in the top 25%. In-memory database throughput registered 111.62 million operations per second on redis SET tests, confirming high execution speed for key-value data structures and memory-intensive access patterns.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote persistent disks for filesystem operations. While this architecture decouples storage capacity from the compute lifecycle, it shifts persistent I/O performance entirely to network-attached block storage. The large allocation of dedicated vCPUs and substantial memory capacity delivers strong resource density without requiring hardware accelerators. The E96as_v6 is aligned with large-scale relational databases, in-memory caches, distributed data analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise-grade memory-heavy processing.

The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector and cryptographic acceleration instructions. In benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier multi-core computing metrics with a stress-ng multi-core result of 147518.16, alongside strong single-core performance of 3077.57 and redis SET throughput of 111.62 million operations per second. The instance includes no onboard local storage and no GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Given its high memory density and extensive parallel compute capabilities, the E96as_v6 is engineered for in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, enterprise data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise application workloads.
